_comment: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) — FY2025 (year ended June 30, 2025)
_source: CBA FY2025 Full Year Results, commbank.com.au, commbank.com.au/newsroom/features/fy2025-financial-results
_note_balance_sheet: Total Assets AUD 1,354B; Net Loans AUD 542B (+8.3%, 40.0% of assets); Total Deposits AUD 930B (68.7%). LDR 58.3% — very low; excess deposits fund large investment and liquid asset portfolio. Australia's largest bank by assets and home loans.
_note_deposits: Australian banks: Transaction/demand ~20%, savings ~35%, term deposits ~45%. CBA has dominant retail deposit franchise. CASA ~55%. Significant wholesale funding also via covered bonds.
_note_exposure: Home loans dominant at ~55% (Australia's largest mortgage lender). Business/Commercial lending ~25%, Personal (cards, personal loans) ~10%, Institutional/corporate ~10%. Property market strength drives mortgage concentration.
_note_credit_quality: NPL ~0.5% — among the world's cleanest loan books. Australia's strong employment, low unemployment and high property collateral values underpin exceptional credit quality. Home loan arrears remain low.
_note_pnl: NIM 2.08% (+9bps YoY from deposit repricing and capital hedge gains). NPAT $10,133M (+7% YoY). ROA 0.78%. ROE 13.7%. Cost-income 48.5% (improving from 50.2% FY24).
_note_capital: CET1 12.3% (June 2025), well above APRA minimum of 10.25%. Australian banks operate under APRA's 'unquestionably strong' capital framework. Tier1 ~13%, Total Capital ~14.5%.
